description: Kuzu Tandir is a timeless Turkish classic featuring incredibly tender, slow-roasted lamb that falls off the bone. Marinated simply and cooked to perfection, this dish offers a rich, succulent flavor profile that is deeply satisfying. It's an impressive centerpiece for any special occasion, embodying the heart of Turkish culinary tradition with every bite.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Pat the lamb shoulder dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix olive oil, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if using. Rub this mixture generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into any crevices. Make a few shallow cuts on the lamb to help the seasoning penetrate.

instructions.title: Sear the Lamb (Optional)
instructions.text: In a large, heavy-bottomed oven-safe pot or Dutch oven, heat a tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb on all sides until nicely browned. This step is optional but adds depth of flavor and color to the final dish. Remove the lamb from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Layer Aromatics
instructions.text: Add the chopped onions and smashed garlic cloves to the same pot. Sauté for about 5-7 minutes until the onions soften and become translucent. If the pot is too dry, add a little more olive oil. You want a fragrant base for your lamb.

instructions.title: Combine and Cover
instructions.text: Place the seared lamb shoulder back into the pot, nestling it on top of the onions and garlic. Pour the hot water or chicken broth around the lamb. Add the fresh rosemary or thyme sprigs if desired. Cover the pot tightly with its lid or with aluminum foil, ensuring a good seal to trap the moisture.

instructions.title: Slow Roast to Perfection
instructions.text: Transfer the covered pot to the preheated oven. Slow roast for 3 hours. After 3 hours, remove the lid or foil and continue roasting for another 30 minutes to 1 hour, or until the lamb is beautifully browned and fork-tender, practically falling off the bone. The internal temperature should reach 70°C (160°F) and stay there for at least 3 minutes, then rest up to 90°C (195°F) for maximum tenderness.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, carefully remove the pot from the oven. Transfer the lamb to a cutting board, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 15-20 minutes before carving or shredding. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a moist and flavorful result. Serve Kuzu Tandir with its pan juices, often alongside rice pilaf or roasted vegetables.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use a bone-in lamb shoulder. The bone adds significant depth and keeps the meat moist during the long cooking process.
Do not rush the slow roasting. The key to Kuzu Tandir's melt-in-your-mouth tenderness is low heat and ample time, allowing connective tissues to break down slowly.
Serve Kuzu Tandir with traditional Turkish rice pilaf (pirinç pilavı) and a fresh salad or roasted root vegetables to complete a truly authentic meal.
